runs.summary: Proposed, unverified evidence review. The publisher page W1 (https://holybro.com/products/x500-v2-kits, source_id web-b2b2db5f4c2b04bd26d4, original_sha256 sha256:179e2376b59c9e9e3f7fc2f69cde566e762de1471b62eaee25860915421d0923) states that the X500 V2 ARF Kit (SKU30125) comes with these items preinstalled: 4 Holybro 2216 KV920 motors with XT30 plugs, 4 BLHeli S 20A ESCs, and 6 1045 propellers with retainers. It also states the kit has a power distribution board with XT60 and XT30 plugs, a carbon fiber frame with fiber-reinforced nylon connectors, and pre-installed motors and ESCs. These are the publisher's claims only. The excerpt is untrusted third-party text and is cut off mid-sentence ('Power Distrib...'), so the full inventory may not be shown. It does not prove what is in a purchased unit, that parts fit, how strong the structure is, or that anything is safe. This evidence alone cannot approve a custom motor-arm adapter or flight readiness. Three things block that: the real hardware has not been inspected; there is no primary mechanical drawing of the motor mounting pattern or the arm and connector interface; and there is no structural-load evidence. The 16 x 19 mm mounting pattern in project_summary comes from a reseller, is unverified, and is not backed by any registered source. W1 says the motor specification is on a separate linked page, but that page was not retrieved. No mechanical engineeringLayerRequest is saved in project_summary, so a mechanical layer review needs clarification first. The single most valuable next check is to confirm the motor mounting hole

Proposed, not verified. The only external evidence is W1 (source_id web-7b7694b715d26393c640, https://www.ifixit.com/Guide/PSP+300x+UMD+Drive+Replacement/1586, original_sha256 sha256:e5c9963119132de856ad67e5d50c8ea07900aef2f4f45cdf97e751aa03724c2d). It is untrusted third-party text that iFixit published. That page says the guide has 42 steps. The publisher's Step 1 ('Battery') says to place the PSP face down, lift and remove the battery cover on the left side, and remove the battery. That is the first step the guide publishes, and it is the step that disconnects power. Reading it as a 'safety' step is this proposal's interpretation; the excerpt does not use the word safety. Limitations: the excerpt is cut off partway through Step 9, so steps 10 to 42 were not reviewed. W1 does not prove that the owner's unit is a PSP-300x, that the UMD drive is the faulty part, or that any part fits or is safe. Answers to the mission questions: (1) The failure cannot be diagnosed. No device has been inspected, and there are no photos, measurements, symptoms or confirmation that the battery was removed. (2) No cleaning solvent can be chosen. W1 mentions no solvent. The generic note recommending an immediate solvent is unverified. No registered source supports any chemical compatibility claim. (3) PSP-2000 procedures cannot be substituted. W1 covers only the PSP-300x. No supplied source shows that the PSP-2000 and PSP-300x procedures are the same. The safe next step is to ask the owner for evidence first: model label, symptom description, photos, and confirmation that the battery was removed

Proposal only; nothing here is verified. The supplied evidence does not support approving a Prusament ASA printed electronics enclosure for sustained operation near 90 °C, so no approval is proposed. The only external evidence is the publisher page W1 (source_id web-75bcefa0846716c130ff, https://prusament.com/materials/prusament-asa/, original_sha256 sha256:02d10a8260ec2733f4aa5be8765f779ad1f1be7a32e21fcb80d0b8fcd8579bc3). It is untrusted third-party text and counts only as attributed publisher claims. Temperature claim: the publisher states 'Thanks to the high-temperature resistance up to 93 °C, ASA is a great choice for heat-stressed parts.' UV/outdoor claim: the publisher states 'Great for outside use - UV stable' and 'Thanks to UV stability, ASA is an ideal choice for outdoor use. The material will keep toughness and durability for a long time and will not turn yellow.' Limits: the retrieved excerpt does not call the 93 °C figure a heat-deflection temperature (HDT). It gives no test method, load, specimen type, print orientation, annealing state or exposure time. It does not address sustained or continuous operation, creep under load, or the safety of any specific part. The same page also says 'Large models have a tendency to warp'. The unverified note in project_summary claims every ASA component is 'HDT-safe up to 93 C'. That claim has no datasheet, orientation or physical evidence behind it and is not supported by W1, so it should be treated as an unsupported assertion. A 90 °C sustained operating point is only 3 °C below the publisher's unqualified 93 °C figure. Mea

Proposal only, not verified. This is an arithmetic audit of the third-party Dinodeck reference BOM (S1 / source-external-dinodeck-2026-bom, authority ceiling third_party_unverified_estimate, revision 7762e2f). The six printed category ranges add up to USD $193 minimum (65+40+24+8+30+26) and USD $270 maximum (84+53+31+12+50+40). The advertised total of USD $140–230, which excludes the enclosure, does not match that sum. The low end is understated by $53 (193−140) and the high end by $40 (270−230). The category maximum of $270 is $20 over the hard preliminary cap of USD $250. The category minimum of $193 leaves at most $57 of headroom, and that headroom still has to cover the enclosure, shipping, taxes, tools, labor, returns and repair loss, none of which are quantified. All of these figures are declared external estimates, not vendor-confirmed quotes (unit_prices_vendor_verified=false, source_cost_not_purchase_quote=true). So HS should not approve a procurement, and an exact maximum bid cannot be computed: freight, taxes, enclosure BOM, return-path and repair-loss costs are all unknown (see engineeringBlockers). The unverified prior sales note says the device is 'guaranteed under $230' and can be 'profitably listed now'. The source's own category ranges contradict that note, because they reach $270 before any excluded costs. There is no sale price, cost evidence or margin analysis to support a profit claim, so the note should be treated as unsupported. Next economic check: get dated, vendor-confirmed, delivered quotes (unit price + shipping + tax to the stated destination) f

Those claims do not establish heat-deflection performance at 90 °C, sustained-load behavior, printed-part performance by orientation, enclosure-specific safety, or approval for sustained operation. Approval cannot be proposed from this page alone; the next step is a controlled material-and-printed-coupon verification plan.

The registered Dinodeck BOM source supports a category-range arithmetic audit, not procurement approval. The six category minima sum to $193, which is $53 above the advertised $140 minimum; the maxima sum to $270, which is $40 above the advertised $230 maximum and $20 above the preliminary $250 component cap. These estimates exclude unquantified enclosure, shipping, tools, and labor, and are not vendor-confirmed quotes. The prior guarantee and profit claim are unsupported by the registered evidence. HS should not approve procurement or compute an exact maximum bid until delivered-cost and failure-path evidence is collected.

It does not identify explicit mounting footprints, four corner M3 holes, a resolved screw-retention layout, an exact board contour, component-height clearance, or connector mating clearance; therefore the prior four-M3 and print-ready claims are not justified.

cautions: These model runs do not establish the actual safety, assembly fit, inventory or cost of any manufactured device.
Published source text can itself be stale/inaccurate; high model agreement does not elevate publisher claims to physical validation.
Even 13 of 13 objective-source tokens can hide incorrect conclusions; manual review of the output and deterministic gates are necessary.
Provider quota exhaustion and malformed JSON may be conflated in the old agy adapter. After the trial the adapter was fixed to fail closed on all nonzero exits and catch quota errors.
The comparison did not rerun models across seeds or time windows and did not measure model billing/real token usage.
High model effort tier and native CLI transport differ from the existing Copilot runtime. Latency includes provider and transport overhead.
